name: MA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean (D+11 PVI) in a Massachusetts seat
Dan Koh's large financial advantage ($4.7M raised vs $0.4M) plus outside support
Open seat with no incumbent on the ballot, adding modest uncertainty
Markets price a Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Democrats holding this D+11 open seat, and Koh's overwhelming fundraising edge and outside support reinforce that. With no polling available, uncertainty stays wide, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected Republican fundraising surge would be the first sign the open seat is genuinely in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Seth Moulton (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Massachusetts' sixth district is an open seat after Seth Moulton left to run for Senate, but it remains firmly Democratic territory with an eleven-point partisan lean. Dan Koh enters the general election with a decisive financial edge, having raised roughly $4.7 million to Micah Jones' $0.4 million, and holds about $2 million in cash while benefiting from outside support with no opposition spending on either side.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 95%, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no general-election polls available, the forecast rests on the seat's lean and the money gap, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the open-seat dynamic keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
